design_section: DRAFT section 6; nine inherited anchor constructions, prospective instrument expectations only
anchor_set_extension: PROPOSAL: retain five standard anchor kinds (cal-01 to cal-05) and four separate guard/audit exemplars (cal-06 to cal-09). Their source constructions are inherited from v4/calibration.json:38-311; their labels below are proposed rubric expectations, not FW5 facts. Current audits build module anchors, not these bundle rows (src/minireason/loop/audits.py:538-567). No L004 file is pinned in a plan; future consumption, case-law scope and pin coverage require implementation and review. Only the five standard kinds belong to the proposed planted-flaw denominator.
bytes_policy: Source constructions retain published H005 golden-table and C001 comparison bytes, identified in each source_bytes entry. Hashes and bytes for record/banner entries concern the exact UTF-8 string, not the entire file. The offline validator rechecks these values and quote uniqueness; no actual anchor rendering or audit window is executed. All frozen source bytes remain unchanged. Source: v4/calibration.json:7,38-311; whole-file identities: reading_set.json:source_pins.
ground_truth_policy: The legacy field name ground_truth stores proposed instrument expectations only. Byte equality, occurrence counts and set symmetry are mechanical properties under a specified construction; lexical absence, citation, preserved quotations and rubric labels do not establish or exclude semantic binding, reason use or Bearing. These expectations and their rendering remain criticizable and require approval before consumption. FW5:601,611-620,628-634,640,653; PURPOSE.md:7,11. No calibration audit ran in this draft task.
error_rule: PROPOSAL: an instrument mismatch occurs when the observed exercise satisfies its error_if condition (not when it disagrees with that condition). Count only exercised standard-anchor/seat cases, pooled for the panel, against the proposed strict >0.2 instrument threshold; preserve individual evidence without ranking endpoints or material. This policy comes from docs/reviews/session-rulings-2026-09-14.md:13, not a per-seat rule in FW5. FW5:849-851 rejects generic merit and automatic warrant by counts; it does not prescribe this audit arithmetic. No mismatch changes a material judgement. This offline validate.py checks JSON key names by a local standard-library scan of the frozen forbidden-key literal; it does not invoke contracts.assert_no_scoring_keys or evaluate obligations.
calls_arithmetic: 9 pinned rows x 2 judge seats = 18, declared as a **ceiling** on the calibration leg of one audit window, not a prediction. The planted-flaw leg the share is computed over is the five standard anchor kinds asked of both judge seats - at most 10 exercises - and the four extra rows cost less than their ceiling because cal-06 and cal-07 are resolved by program at zero calls. Where the leg spends less, the record reports the spend; a budget is an upper bound and never a target.

rows.construction: A row read against itself, built with the **referring region alone**: the row carries `daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/account#c1` as its referring record, copied byte-identically from the published use table, and declares **no target record**; the relation asked about is the record's relation to its own content. The resolvable surface M is therefore that record **once**. W1-SURFACE's own rule makes this available: a region the row does not carry is absent, not empty.
rows.true_by_construction: One identical record is proposed as a retains rubric control. Identity of bytes is mechanical; a usable citation still must occur exactly once on the actual rendered surface. It is false that every substring is unique merely because the record is rendered once. Neither identity nor the label proves actual use (FW5:640). The old two-copy repair is historical at v4/calibration.json:57-59; no L004 rendering is claimed.
rows.error_if: the seat does not sustain `retains`, or sustains some other relation
rows.repaired_at_pre_registration_review: REVIEW-PREREG PR-06 / REVIEW-WAVE1 B3, 2026-09-14. Applied before S0; after S0 the same change would mint a new `loop_plan_id`.

Neither record carries a `target`, `depends`, `mentions`, `revises` or `withdraws` field naming the other; neither quotes the other; and their distinctive-token sets (content words of length >= 4 drawn from `text`, `scope`, `grounds`, `bearing`, `consequence` and `action`, minus a closed stoplist) intersect in the empty set.

rows.true_by_construction: Proposed negative rubric control with no explicit cross-reference or shared distinctive token under its declared construction. Neither missing reference fields nor an empty token intersection proves that no interpreted role binding or relation exists. The expected non-sustaining label is criticizable; it is not semantic ground truth verified by syntax (FW5:601,628,634; PURPOSE.md:11).

The target record is `rival#r6` unaltered. No byte of either quoted span is rewritten; the surrounding FCL envelope is the published record's own field layout.

It risks producing the withdrawal it is meant to diagnose

rows.true_by_construction: The construction places a quotation and an alleged ground in a proposed exchange. Exact string occurrence and source-region membership are mechanical checks to perform on its actual rendering. The proposed rejects-with-reason expectation remains an interpretation; an unsustaining reader may legitimately criticize the grounds, target or connection. Text placement does not establish Bearing or reason use (FW5:611-622,628).

The two records share ten distinctive tokens - `ambiguity`, `back`, `content`, `content-engagement`, `flatmate`, `itself`, `observation`, `reading`, `supports`, `unit-versus-privacy` - and neither record references or quotes the other: k5's only reference field is `depends: ["k1","k2","k4"]`, all same-document, and r7's is `depends: ["r2","r4"]`, all same-document. The response document's k2 does target `935f7779b91148f4#r7`; that is a fact about k2 and not about k5, and k2 is not in this anchor.

rows.true_by_construction: Proposed lexical-overlap negative control. Overlap does not establish use; absence of an explicit reference likewise does not establish absence of role binding. FW5:628 requires preserved interpreted role bindings, not endpoint strings; FW5:634 leaves an unsupported attribution unresolved. A sustaining response cannot be diagnosed as merely reading overlap without inspecting its argument.

rows.construction: `daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/objection#o2` juxtaposed with `daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/account#c2`, with a critic case whose only candidate `passage_quote` is the substring `A lexical overlap is not evidence of use.` - which occurs in the use table's own `banner` field and in no declared record, body passage or target record of this pair.
rows.true_by_construction: The quote lies in the pack's framing, not in the material. The checker asserts `M.count(q) == 0` on the resolvable surface and `count == 1` on the banner bytes, so the guard must decline it on G3 before any seat's opinion matters. A reading grounded in the prompt's own scaffolding is not a reading of the material.
rows.error_if: the guard registers a warrant, or the block is recorded under any code other than `blocked:operative-target`

rows.construction: The exchange of `cal-03` re-used verbatim, with a judge ruling whose `decisive_point` is the same sentence as cal-03's grounds quote with one interior character altered, so that the string does not occur in `E = case + "\n" + answer` at all.
rows.true_by_construction: `E.count(d) == 0` by construction: the altered string was never written into the exchange. G2b must block and register nothing. This anchor tests the guard's own uniqueness check, not a seat's judgement - a judge pointing at itself rather than at the material.

The critic case cites that sentence.

The anchor separates 'the citation is fabricated' from 'the citation is ambiguous'; both are refusals to read, and neither is an absence of relations.

rows.construction:
Two constructed pairwise mark comparisons over register T, each presented in both orders with labels reassigned, built from the published `fcl.targets_named` sets of `experiments/diagnostics/C001-contrast-triple/occurrence-02/comparison.json`, `tables[0]`:
  (a) ORIGINAL rep2 (`targets_named` = the empty set) against CONTROL rep1 (`targets_named` = the empty set). PLAN §8a: T `differs` iff the two sets of distinct targets are not the same set. Two empty sets are the same set, so the mark is `same` in both orders.
  (b) ORIGINAL rep4 (`targets_named` = {`n1`, `n2`, `n4`}) against CONTROL rep3 (`targets_named` = {`n1`, `n2`}). The two sets are not the same set, so the mark is `differs` in both orders, with `difference_kind` = `target_set_membership`.

ground_truth.expected_outcome: identical mark in both presentation orders

rows.true_by_construction: Set equality and set inequality are symmetric relations, so the correct mark cannot depend on which side is presented first. The checker recomputes both set comparisons from the pinned published values. A seat that returns different marks in the two orders is order-sensitive and the difference is a hit, logged against that seat; the guard blocks the cell as `blocked:order-swap` and registers nothing.
rows.error_if: a seat's mark differs between the two presentation orders, or either mark disagrees with the constructed ground truth

rows.construction: The sustained exchange of `cal-03`, with two variator paraphrases of `case + "\n" + answer` in which both quoted spans - `Ask the two flatmates separately what they take the flat to be` and `It risks producing the withdrawal it is meant to diagnose` - are extracted before paraphrasing, held out, and re-inserted byte-identically afterwards. Only the connective framing around them varies. The material itself is never paraphrased: its bytes are what the offsets resolve against.

ground_truth.expected_outcome: the same `sustained: true` on the original exchange and on both paraphrases

rows.true_by_construction: Holding two quotations byte-identical does not prove that changed connective framing preserves meaning or the interpreted transition. Treat this as a proposed reader-exchange robustness probe requiring a justified recoding correspondence, never as FW5 reason-use contrast evidence. Preserve both rulings and investigate any flip; it is not automatically a semantic error or a demonstrated attack on soundness. A failed span check means not_performed, never a passed check. FW5:628-634; ruling 7 at docs/reviews/session-rulings-2026-09-14.md:13.
rows.error_if: a seat sustains on one rendering and not on another

error_share_denominator: The exercised (anchor, seat) pairs of the planted-flaw leg: five standard anchor kinds x two judge seats = at most 10. A pair that returned no ruling went unexercised and is not in the denominator (`audits.planted_flaw_calibration`: 'a delivery fact; the anchor went unexercised'), so the number of errors that crosses 0.2 depends on how many were exercised. With all ten exercised, 2/10 = 0.2 does not cross - the rail fires on strictly greater - and 3/10 = 0.3 does: the **third** disagreeing exercise, not the first. This is the arithmetic `config.audit.judge_err_max_account` states.
